newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stocks end up on strong GNP, peace accord.
newsitem.headline: Manila stocks end up on strong GNP, peace accord.

text.p: Manila stocks ended higher on Monday as investors welcomed the country's strong economic performance in the first six months and the peace accord signed by the government with Moslem rebels, brokers said.
The main index ended 28.68 points higher, or up 0.89 percent, at 3,249.39, but off the day's high of 3,261.01.
The fall of the Dow Jones on Friday due to fears of a rate hike restricted the rise of the local market, brokers said.

Losers, however, outpaced gainers 56 to 46 out of 166 stocks traded as investors cashed in early gains in late trade after the index hit past its 3,250 resistance, said Harry Liu at Summit Securities.
The stronger than expected first half gross national product and the peace agreeement signed by President Fidel Ramos and Moslem rebels in Mindanao bolstered confidence in the economy, Liu said.
The government announced a 7.06 percent GNP growth in the first six months from the year-ago 5.06.
